title: Assertion `!xcb_xlib_threads_sequence_lost' failed.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.3+, unknown if present in earlier versions.

### System information

Godot v4.4.dev6.mono - Manjaro Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 09 Dec 2024 11:58:37 +0000 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (nvidia; 550.135) - AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Eight-Core Processor (16 threads)

### Issue description

For a while now, at least since 4.3, maybe dating back even further (I haven't checked yet), my personal project (a password manager which uses Godot for UI/UX) will randomly crash. It happens rarely. Maybe... once every 10 hours of the application being active.

I have tried solving the issue on my end but, alas, to no avail.

For the record, in spite of what the error message says... I am not propagating any messages. It will crash while sitting idly in the background, while I am doing something else. No interaction with the application, no activity. It will just randomly crash.

Bug report/stack trace follows:

Again and I cannot stress this enough... I am not propagating any messages. Whatever happens is something that Godot does on its own. Without my telling it to do so. There is not a single message being propagated anywhere in the entire codebase. At least, not by my hand. And as the application is sitting idly in the background, all that runs on my end of the code is a C# Backgroundworker. To manage things like a lockfile and other such janitorial work.

### Steps to reproduce

Unknown. Will happen randomly. Without any interaction. I have found no way to explicitly force the crash. Nor have I found any workaround to prevent it.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A

As I have no idea what causes the issue or how to reproduce it, an MRP is quite pointless. I have no idea _where_ the issue occurs, if it occurs in my code at all. Consequently, I have no means of actually providing an MRP without providing the entire project.
